title: TypeScript: typing props, generics, and the component that takes anything

videos.script:
TypeScript has checked every component in this course. Today it checks things a test would struggle to find.

{{props}} First the contract a props type is: a wrong type, a missing prop, each caught at its line before anything runs.

{{union}} Then a status that cannot lie. The planner could be loading and still claim to have no courses. A discriminated union gives each status only the fields that mean something in it, and the compiler finds three places that never checked.

{{narrow}} Then narrowing, once, where the planner already decided what to draw.

{{never}} Then the case nobody handled: a fourth status, and a line with never in it that turns a future blank page into an error today.

{{generic}} And last, a component that takes anything: a generic list, whose item type nobody writes and the compiler still knows.
